topic.title: Why Criticism Sticks and Praise Doesn't

copy.thumb_scene: Wick stands upright on a plain white studio background, arms loose at his sides, holding a single crumpled note in one hand and a stack of clean white cards in the other, his eyes fixed forward with a calm, unreadable expression, the crumpled note visibly worn compared to the untouched stack.
copy.send_to: the friend who replays one bad comment for weeks

caption:
Most people think hitting a certain number of reps just makes you mentally tougher.

It doesn't.

The ladder is not about reps. It is about the gap between how many times the brain registers a loss versus how many it needs to register a win before it stops flinching.

The hidden rule is this: the mind upgrades its threat filter through Behaviour, and that filter is what every financial decision quietly runs through before you even see the numbers.

Miss this and every salary bump still feels temporary. Every bill feels like proof. The math of your life keeps getting read through a nervous system that was calibrated on the worst day you had last year.

Sharpen the filter or the filter runs you.

When did you last notice a compliment landing with the same weight as a criticism? Drop it in the replies.

Light one. Pass it on. 🕯️
